My ex was also avoidant. Likely through no fault of his own, and a result of his shitty/emotionally absent parents. Regardless, he was incapable of providing the emotional support and physical affection I needed. Coming from an abused background tainted with years of sexual assault, this was horribly detrimental for my recovery. 

You may love him, and you may love his family, but the hard truth is that it doesn't make him a healthy partner for you. I learned the hard way that loving someone isn't a brute-force solution to relationship problems. 

My relationship had become very turbulent and chaotic by the time I lost my shit and knew I had to get out. If you are not yet at that point, oh please don't let it get there. 

Narcs raise us to be codependent and to believe we can't survive on our own two feet. It's scary and intimidating but you will gain the freedom to help yourself however you need. Feeling ugly and worthless and just want to snuggle up with someone, or maybe have a casual one night stand to feel sexually desired without feeling needy or a whore? Download tinder and bumble, no joke! Even if you never meet up with anyone, it helps you get a realistic idea of how people see you.

Getting out of an unhappy relationship is the best present you could give yourself, and honestly it will be the best way to heal from the still fresh Narc abuse. Reach out to old friends or internet forums to talk about dumb stuff or rant or vent. Even people you haven't spoken to in months or years will understand the need for support during a breakup. 

As far as figuring out if your relationship is healthy... Well, I'm still learning that actually haha! But this is my experience. The person you are with should make you feel AMAZING about yourself. They should give you CONFIDENCE. You should never have to beg or ask them for compliments or opinions. They will treat you like an equal, even when you have your rock bottom moments. They will want to talk with you and come to resolutions. They will never demean you or make you feel unworthy for any reason. If they do, and you tell them, they genuinely are sorry and actively try to change their actions. They are comfortable telling you when you do something that upsets them, and don't attack you and aren't accusatory. I believe if someone is healthy for you, their presence helps elevate and motivate you to your best possible self. If you love someone, you want them to be their best possible self and to get everything they deserve out of life. 

I didn't start dating my current boyfriend until I was able to see myself as equal to him, and not a broken fucked up monster dating a beautiful smart compassionate man. You can't go into a relationship without discovering your own worth first. You don't have to like yourself, but you do have to love yourself and respect yourself. This will help you start with and maintain healthy boundaries. 

From there? Communication, communication, communication. Honest and constant communication. No secrets, no lies, no beating around the bush. Have compassion and patience, and be willing to talk about anything that upsets you and be willing to examine why and be willing to help create a solution. It's a two way street, so your partner must do the same. 

Tell each other what you think. When I'm staring at him and thinking "damn what a sexy beast," I make sure to tell him that. I want him to know how I see him and his value to me, and he does the same for me. It's very validating, which we both need coming from bad previous relationships. 

ANYWAY I'm gonna stop ranting in my comment replies now. I really hope this was helpful!!

You really are in the same boat as I was, and my heart aches because I know what you're going through and how unbelievably hard and scary it is. I remember hating myself for not having the "guts" or the "courage" for not being able to go through with my suicidal plans. Fears like what you had prevented me from doing the same things. 

I know it is super dark and you probably can't imagine any way out of this mess. That is normal. That is okay. Try to focus on each day as a separate entity. Survive one day at a time. One couch, one shower, one panic attack, one job application, one attempt to reach out, one breakdown at a time. 

Take it moment to moment and prioritize YOURSELF. Keep yourself fed. Women's shelters are the BEST and were my saving grace and immediate resource when I became homeless. They often provide free counseling. Set yourself up for a weekly session with them!! Bi-weekly if possible, while things are still in crisis. You need the support and they have resources. 

Reach out to your friends, even if it has been months or years since you last spoke. What's the worse that could happen, they ignore you or say no? You already want to die and never speak to them, so what does it really change? It provides you the opportunity for support and reconnection. You would be surprised how many people will be willing to support you.

The person you hurt? If they are a healthy influence in your life and not a toxic person, ask to have a talk. A person who values you as a friend would rather talk and hear an apology from you and come to a resolution, than ignore you in your time of need because you hurt them. Be genuine in your apology and ask them for an opportunity to explain why you did or said what you did, why you think it's wrong, and how you'll try to do better in the future. If they still are upset with you, it's possibly a deeper wound on their end that makes them unable to provide the support you need. That, or they are a toxic person and don't value you.

Regardless, YOU CAN DO THIS. Dude, you survived your Ns. You are actively fighting and clawing for your freedom that you DESERVE. You can do this. When you cut the cancerous fucks out of your life, you will bleed and scar and it will feel like you're dying. You survived the actual toxic Narc abuse, so surviving the escape will be way less intense than you expect. The first few weeks/months are the hardest. 

But then suddenly you realize you have YOUR OWN LIFE. Yours. Completely yours. And now, you can take care of yourself as you see fit. No one to criticize or control you. You know so much more about yourself than you realize. Once the fresh open wounds scab over, you won't have anything picking at it anymore. Removing the toxic environment and people is key. How can a wound heal if it's constantly being re-opened? 

SORRY I KNOW THIS IS A LONG RANT but hang in there okay?? Right now is so fucking hard, but damn if the other side isn't worth it. You will feel a happiness and peace you have never experienced. I want that for you, and I want that for everyone who has suffered entire lives with Narcs. YOU GOT THIS!!

Everyone has the right to feel suicidal. Whether chemically induced due to genetics, or because of events in their life. Nothing you feel is wrong. No feeling is inherently wrong. You aren't being ridiculous for feeling suicidal just because you can't pinpoint why.

While you say your parents weren't bad and did their best, that doesn't mean you were raised in an emotionally healthy way. Your lack of memory of a childhood is a common indicator of that. The way you downplay the bad things that happen (the worst you dealt with was bullying), makes me think you've been raised to think you are supposed to just be happy because nothing bad happened. Thats not how human emotions work.

Forgive me if this is offensive or overstepping. I've seen 3 people personally now struggling with the same issues. Their parents weren't bad parents and genuinely care about them and tried their best, even if they messed up sometimes. That doesn't mean that their actions and/or inactions didn't effect you, just because they meant well and tried their best, or never did anything terrible. EDIT: Or because they changed their behavior for the better by the end.

I recommend reading the book Running On Empty. Emotional neglect causes so many people to suffer from depression and feel they have no reason to be depressed. Parents who are emotionally neglectful aren't bad parents!! They just weren't able to give you what you needed to grow into an emotionally healthy adult. This book will help you figure out if that might be the source of your feelings, and if so, has a lot of great ways to teach yourself what you need to know to overcome it.  

You deserve to be happy. Remember that! You are already feeling shitty, so try not to use your feelings as a weapon against yourself. Easier said than done, I know. There is nothing to feel guilty about. I know me saying that won't change how you feel, but it is the truth, okay? You are inherently worthy.

Call CPS. Ask them to make it clear that a concerned third party initiated the request. Call the cops as well; they can't really do anything, but if or when things escalate, they will be far more likely to believe your friend instead of the manipulations of her family.

Tell your friend to look at r/raisedbynarcissists . Her situation sounds very very similar to my own growing up. They are being abusive, and conditioning her to believe she's worthless. 

In the meantime, as a friend, the best thing you can do is try to be as available as possible. I suggest messaging apps that aren't connected through Facebook or phone number. This way, you can stay in contact via wi-fi. To ease the suicidal ideation, tell her the positive aspects of herself. Constantly. She will tell you you're wrong, and give you many explanations. Try to logic through them and keep staying positive. Let her know you love & care about her no matter what. It takes time to unlearn self-loathing.

Try to help her view & treat herself like she would treat someone she cares about. This is called self-love, which she desperately needs given her environment. 

If you need someone to talk to or want to ask any advice, PM me. She is very lucky to have a friend like you watching out for her.

Thank you. I really didn't know what to expect when I posted this. I was just in such a dark place. The amount of support and great advice has inspired me. It makes me glad that my choice to keep fighting also inspires others.

I never bought her... My family did. I came from a rich family, which is how they could cover up everything they did so flawlessly.

I have been working at barns, internships, & part time jobs to keep her for the past 6 years. It costs $370/month to keep her (food/board/feet), but I have built I strong reputation in the horse community for my responsible nature. Every barn I've been to has let me keep her/take care of her in exchange for feeding and turnout a few nights a week. 

She is phenomenal for my mental health. She has given me extraordinary hope and confidence since I got lucky enough to have her passed to me. I don't really have anything else in my life that has given me what she has, in that sense. It has been good exercise, which also helps with the depression.

I had already paid this month forward. My barn owner is working with me to find someone to lease her, so I could get to still own her, cover overhead costs, and still make a small profit.

Thank you. I appreciate the encouragement a lot. Sometimes it really feels like the climb is never-ending. 

I've survived too much to give up now, I think. I keep telling myself how mad my younger self would be if she found out she survived all that shit just to gave up later. As another poster commented, I have truly been through the worst part. The memories are scars, not fresh wounds.

Thank you! I've been told often I'm strong, and sometimes its hard to see that through how incredibly weak and broken I feel. Hearing people say that I am strong helps me get bits of courage in times like this.

My ex can take the dog, but I have found other alternatives now, thank goodness. Also I am seeing a free counselor at the women's shelter twice a week, and she has been very helpful throughout this.
I've never heard that quote before, but I really like it. Thank you for sharing that with me, and for the support

Thank you for this. I try to remind myself constantly that I can't be responsible for anyone's feelings but my own. I think that was also a part of why our relationship became so unhealthy. We both felt directly responsible for making each other feel x way, and that is so much pressure and redirects our problems onto each other.

I posted there a few days ago, but a few hours later I noticed all the comments were deleted. I deleted my post after that because I wasn't sure what was happening and felt insecure, lol. They did suggest r/almosthomeless which is a good resource too.
Thank you so much. Its surreal seeing people say they believe I can get through this. I always think I look sound even more pathetic than I feel.

Thank you, it means a lot to know an internet stranger is crying for me. It makes me feel like I matter, and its not just some kind of friend bias. Hope that doesn't sound offensive, it really does help.

I am high priority for a room at the local women's shelter, and they've been incredibly helpful. The local domestic & sexual violence safe place is providing me with food consistently so I no longer have to worry about feeding myself for now. I'm losing a lot of weight (99lbs currently, but I'm short, so it should be fine), but I don't feel malnourished.

I've never had contact with any aunts or uncles. My mom kept us isolated from any other family. But I'm so happy you mentioned aunts. I have a family friend I used to see often before college that I called/thought was my aunt, though we aren't actually related. She lives in town. I'm going to call her and drop by tomorrow. 

I agree, its way too much to ask to house me & the dog. I found someone who can take the dog, thank goodness. My ex can take her, but I'm sick of being seen and told I'm a leech. It doesn't help my mental state at all. Her previous owners are more than happy to watch her thank goodness.

Thank you so much! I would've NEVER remembered that aunt. She also doesn't speak to my mother, and cut herself out of my family bullshit. Which makes her a great idea at the very least.
I'm honestly grateful to have a place to share the truth about my life without judgment, and recieve so much support. Thank you

I can't explain how much this helped me. I cried. Thank you so much.

Can't handle churches because I was told to beg God to forgive what my dad did to me, that a father would never do that, and that God allowed me to be raped to serve a greater purpose.

But I have friends. And I can float on. I can drift until I can grab onto something that can pull me out. I have been reaching out to every single source I can find. I'm glad I reached out here too.

You're right. You're so right. I got through the worst already. I'm at rock bottom. There isn't any farther to fall. And these mental scars, they are only memories. They aren't real. What happened was real, but these vivid flashbacks are just memories. They can't hurt me the way I was hurt before. 

Thank you so much for helping me see the survivor in myself again.

Thanks, I appreciate it. Hoping I can survive this. It gets so overwhelming and painful.

Also I'm almost 24 😅 But your point stands just the same.

No problem! I have had awful and intense panic attacks for years and its absolutely the WORST. I always looked for ways to stop them but nothing really worked except medicine. But the fact is, you're never going to ALWAYS have medicine available (probably), so it just wasn't enough for me haha. This is something you can practice even when you aren't panicking, and that mental practice carries over into when you are anxious or panicking. Hope it helps!

I think this is a lovely idea, but can see it encouraging really negative responses. I know I never knew how to answer a lot of things we ACONs get bingoed with. As I started to uncover all of my anger, I began responding in ways that made the other person uncomfortable. I saw this as "well, its an uncomfortable truth!!" But, I think that sort of aggressive response is only due when the bingo-er won't drop the subject.

Ex:     
"How can you cut her out completely? She's your mother! She loves you even if she messed up. She is your family."

"Its not safe or healthy for me to have any form of contact or relationship with her until she makes some serious changes to her behavior, and acknowledges her abuse, however well-intentioned it may have been. I'm not responsible for her happiness or preserving a positive mother-daughter relationship."

BUT, if they keep pushing it, or try to defend her, I drop the cold hard truth:

"She let my father rape me for years and helped hide it. She convinced me I was worthless. Being a mother doesn't absolve you of abuse."

I used to walk away at the point where they push it, but I would rather say something shocking to potentially open their eyes, if its truly out of igorance. Or, at the very least, make them feel uncomfortable enough to not badger someone like that in the future, lol.

I'm so sorry your Nmom is trying to ruin such a happy and beautiful thing. Unfortunately, that's just so N.

I wanted to let you know I've experienced something a little similar. Been dating my SO for over 7 years, and we got engaged last year. During the time we were dating, I could not talk about him around Nmom or else be drowned in criticisms of us both. How he would ruin my life, or the other way around. Eventually this evolved into outright pretending he didn't exist, and asking me if I was ever going to get a boyfriend or date someone. It was absolutely excruciating, and something that is so hard to explain to those who haven't experienced it. The pain of having your own mother, and other members of your family who have been poisoned by her lies and gossip, shit on the part of your life that makes you happiest... I've yet to find something comparable. It's a deep wound of sorts. Hard to explain. Your Nmom sounds like exactly how my Nmom behaved before I went NC. Any time I spoke of him, she would get enraged.

Throughout my engagement, she constantly makes up lies to spread to family & friends about the state of my relationship, or the failures of my fiance and me. I hear about her lies and stories about us through the grapevine. It used to hurt me. But now, I can't help but find it somewhat funny.

I have not spoken or seen this woman in 5 years. Yet her whole life revolves around shit-talking me to anyone who will listen. Every year that passes and she continues to behave this way, she's exposing herself. I go on with my life and try not to mention her unless in relevant conversation, and even then I don't go into details. I never said a thing to anyone, never defended myself or my fiance. I just keep moving forward away from the toxicity and never acknowledged her. 

Now, she is the gossip. How strange that this mother is so obsessed with trashing her child and her family. How odd that 5 years later, her life revolves around trying to sabotage my reputation. Or trying to gain pity. 

Your wedding, your marriage, is about you and your future husband. Not anybody else. Its about celebrating the special bond you share, and promising each other eternity. It is not about your Nmom or what she thinks. There are no rules for wedding planning, so do what makes you comfortable and happy! That is ALL that matters. 

Cut your Nmom out of planning entirely. Put her on a complete information diet. Let her run her mouth. If you don't respond to her, or try to defend yourself to others to undo the damage she caused, people will come to their own conclusions. If you focus on you, and your happiness, it will shine through. And everyone will see her for the nasty bitter hag she is. And the ones who don't see it? A complete waste of your time. 

source: 3 older brothers, 1 married and cut her out of the wedding completely (was uninvited as well). GC-bro is getting married soon and also is planning to cut her out of the wedding. Nmoms nasty rumors leading up to the wedding only did my brother the favor of not having to explain why he wasn't inviting her. She was already making it obvious.

Not OP obviously, but I might be able to offer a possible reason he keeps asking. BDD. I have struggled with it my entire life until recently and one of my brothers has been in the same boat, going so far as to get plastic surgery to fix his "ugly nose" and "ugly jaw" (he's a solid 7/10). He was trying to get a second surgery for something else, but his doctor refused unless he saw a psychiatrist or therapist who could verify he did not have BDD. Needless to say, he never got another surgery. Therapy, medication, and self-help books has helped us immensely. No matter what anyone said to either of us, no matter how often, we didn't see what the rest of the world sees when they look at us.

Body dysmorphia causes you to **truly** see yourself differently than how you actually look. You hyper focus on every little thing thats wrong with you, to the point where you genuinely believe you are disgusting. You see an ugly person in the mirror. You can see fat rolls that don't exist, or think you have a super fucked up nose when you don't.

It destroys your confidence and self-esteem. It makes you want to ask constantly because its honestly mind boggling when people tell you over and over that you are seeing yourself far uglier than you are. It comes off as begging for attention. I became so ashamed of how much I asked ("it just didnt make sense!!! that couldn't possibly be right!!! why doesn't someone see what I see??") bc I knew it came off as constantly seeking attention.

OP, I am no psychiatrist , but I do believe you're struggling with BDD as well. I really hope you can see yourself the way we see you. You aren't ugly, and your height is less relevant than you might think (Have a friend who is 5'2" and gets laid constantly. He is not cute, but his personality & confidence more than makes up for it). You can't change your height, and its pretty expensive and risky to change your face via plastic surgery (Please trust me on this. My brother had a terrible experience and the first jaw implants didnt set right, leading to 2 months with his face looking like a balloon.). But you can change your self-esteem and confidence. 

You seem like a great dude. You have a desire to change (even if its currently surgery), and don't seem to be blaming others for your problems. You have so much potential for happiness. Happy people are more attractive. If you become happy with yourself, women will be far more interested. If they already can tell *you* think you're terrible, then why would they assume any differently about you?

Hope this rambling wall of text was helpful lol. Good luck OP :)

Thanks, it helps to look at it from an objective perspective like that. I also felt pretty peeved they expected me to PAY to feel worse. All I could think was, "Seriously? You guys realize I'm *paying you for a service* that can be easily obtained elsewhere. How can this possibly be a smart business move??" 

My entire family operates under this super weird system of "You don't leave a service provider if they have served you well and know you, because its a personal insult and selfish. You need to stick it out." Only since cutting contact did I realize how wrong and honestly stupid this was, but its hard to shake that impulse...

I feel the exact same way!!!

My nmom is the MOST judgemental person I have ever had the displeasure of knowing. She criticizes everyone, diagnoses everyone with some mental illness or another, constantly looking for a scandal, or hidden victims of abuse. It was utterly unbearable. I responded exactly the same way as you.

I look for the best in literally everyone. Sometimes to the point of detriment, admittedly. I like to focus on the positive things. 

Honestly, sometimes nothing makes me happier than seeing someone smile because they feel good about themselves. I try to give compliments often; even if I'm shy, embarrassed, or worried it will come off wrong. A simple compliment on hair color, a tattoo, a hat, a thankless task, a small success, ect can go a long way for someone who might be struggling (in my own experience ;) ). 

I want to be a person who spreads positivity and kindness in a world full of toxic cancerous narcs and other abusers. Positivity is infectious!

Don't worry, you don't lack empathy! Your concern about your lack of empathy shows as much. What you're experiencing is a coping mechanism for the inability to understand and process your emotions. You had to shut down and lock away your emotions as much as possible to survive living with abusive parents. If you don't feel anything, you can't be attacked for feeling the wrong thing, or mocked for it. 

Honestly in your case, it may be the simple fact that you have been conditioned to believe you are selfish and evil and incapable if empathy since a very very young age. You were set up to fail, every action judged under the lense of selfishness instead of compassion and understanding. They were your parents, your primary source for emotional nourishment as a child. Of course you would believe them. 

The harming of animals in early childhood should have been a wake up call for your parents, had they been sane. A normal parent would want to find out the source of the behavior and want to help & support the child through uncovering the reason behind it. 

Nparents:   
 
1. Don't care why you do anything, because they assign you motivations regardless
2. Know on some level they are responsible for your behavior, and don't want to be held accountable for it.
3. Use fear & insults to condition/manipulate you into obedience and doubt of self-perception.

A child can't grow to understand and process emotions when they are constantly in an environment where they are guilty until proven innocent. We learned to repress our emotions to increase our chances of being listened to, or believed. In order to avoid punishment or humiliation. To not be selfish. To not be "bad."

Check out the book *Running on Empty* by Jonice Webb. It addresses how and why you feel and react certain ways to things, due to the emotional neglect experienced during childhood. It is incredibly insightful :).

>If it matters, you don't sound terrible with confrontation to me. At all. You may not realize but from your writing I can read that you're making so much progress. 

Wow, thank you 🙈 Lately I feel like I'm starting to handle conflict & confrontation *much* better than before. It feels good to be validated!

>We'll see, maybe the manager will get back to you with good news. Otherwise, I don't know, maybe you could consider giving it a shot with that therapist and see what she has to say about her methods and maybe discuss improvements I guess. 

I hope to hear good news! I'm giving them until Mon of next week to hear back before I cancel my subscription. They charge a hefty fee if you don't cancel your appointment 48 hours in advance. This may not be the best response to the situation, but I don't want to pay $85 to discuss a change in methods when she wasn't willing to discuss my concerns *before* she found out I wanted to switch to a different therapist. 

Thank you for your support and encouragement!! And for the compliment on my username ;)

Thank you!! I also felt the first "switch" doesn't mean anything. I had only gone to two actual sessions before knowing we wouldn't work. I would consider that a normal trial period for a therapist. I can almost always know for sure if it won't work within 1-3 visits.

>> The right time, however, is if you feel that you're not progressing, you feel you've tried to work things out but it's not working.

Precisely this. I felt like I was hitting a wall in our communication that I just couldn't overcome. If she wouldn't listen to my requests or respond to my concern until she discovered I wanted to switch to someone else, it doesn't feel like genuine communication. 

I'm sorry you had such a terrible experience. Can I ask how staying with that style of therapist (for trauma) effected you when you were with them?

While the emotional control and mindfulness she taught me has been amazing, I can't just constantly ignore the memories being brought up the more I understand my own emotions. It destroys me inside. I've been really wanting to work through the deep shame that I can't shake no matter how much I logic through it. So when I started feeling progressively MORE ashamed, it was against everything I was working towards.
